description: Key facts for this chapter, written by hand from the chapter text. Every entry links to the section that explains it.

people.name: Gaius Duilius
people.text: Consul who won Rome’s first naval victory, at Mylae in 260 BC.

people.name: Regulus
people.text: Consul who invaded Africa in 256 BC and was captured in 255 BC.

people.name: Hamilcar Barca
people.text: Carthaginian general in Sicily from 247 BC; he later led his veterans to Spain.

people.name: Catulus
people.text: Consul whose fleet won the final battle, at the Aegates Islands in 241 BC.

people.name: Polybius
people.text: Greek historian, our main source for the war.

dates.text: Roman legions cross to Sicily: the war begins.
Carthage’s relief army is beaten at Akragas.
Rome builds a fleet; Duilius wins at Mylae.
Cape Ecnomus, perhaps the largest sea battle ever; Regulus lands in Africa.
Regulus is captured; a storm sinks most of Rome’s fleet.
Carthage’s greatest naval victory, at Drepana.
Hamilcar Barca takes command in Sicily.
Battle of the Aegates Islands; peace; Sicily becomes Rome’s first province.
Rome forces Carthage to give up Sardinia and Corsica.

terms.english: an overseas territory under a Roman governor
